requirements.text: Health endpoint returns status and tool count GET /api/health returns JSON with status 'ok' and tools count as integer.
List tools returns categorized tool listing GET /api/tools returns JSON with count, categories, and tools array sorted by category then name.
Run calculator returns 400 on invalid JSON body POST /api/calc with malformed JSON returns 400 with error 'invalid JSON'.
Run calculator returns 400 on invalid sanitized params POST /api/calc with parameters that fail validation returns 400 with error message from _sanitize_params.
Run calculator returns 400 on calculator domain errors POST /api/calc with inputs that cause ValueError, ZeroDivisionError, KeyError, or TypeError returns 400 with actionable error message.
Run calculator returns 400 on unexpected calculator exception POST /api/calc with inputs that cause an unexpected exception returns 400 with generic error 'calculation failed'.
Run calculator returns result on valid calculator and params POST /api/calc with valid calculator name and parameters returns 200 with calculator name and result.
API NAV returns 400 on invalid scheme code GET /api/nav with code that is not all digits or longer than 9 characters returns 400 with error 'invalid scheme code'.
API NAV returns 400 on invalid query GET /api/nav with empty q or q longer than 80 characters returns 400 with error 'query must be 1–80 characters'.
API FX returns 400 on invalid currency codes GET /api/fx with base or symbols not matching _CCY_RE returns 400 with error 'invalid currency code'.
API Quote returns 400 on invalid symbol GET /api/quote with symbol not matching _SYMBOL_RE returns 400 with error 'invalid symbol'.
Payload size limit on /api endpoints POST /api/* with content-length greater than 16384 returns 413 with error 'payload too large'.

Security headers added to every HTTP response Every HTTP response includes x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy, strict-transport-security, cross-origin-opener-policy, and content-security-policy headers.

skippedLevels.reason: All P0 and P1 behaviors involve HTTP request/response handling, middleware, or external I/O (payload size check, security headers, JSON parsing, query validations). No pure-logic-only scenarios exist for these requirements; existing unit tests in tests/ (e.g., test_tvm.py) cover isolated calculator logic but are not P0/P1. Writing additional unit tests would duplicate integration coverage.
The application has no browser-accessible UI; it is a JSON-over-HTTP API only. All functionality is accessed via API calls, making E2E browser testing impossible and unnecessary.
